# BLUETTI AC200L — Best 2kWh RV Power Station

<row align="start" gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station front view" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="124px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **<Entity value="BLUETTI AC200L" category="product" disambig="2048Wh portable LiFePO4 power station"/>**

    <title color="success" size="2xl" tabularNums={true}>$854.05</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Regular listed price: $899 · Promo code: AFF5OFF</text>
    <text color="success" size="sm" weight="medium">Reported in stock at BLUETTI official store</text>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Price checked October 27–31, 2026</text>
    [View deal at BLUETTI Official Store](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)
  </box>

### Why I'd choose it

| Specification | BLUETTI AC200L |
|---|---:|
| Battery capacity | 2,048 Wh |
| Battery chemistry | LiFePO4 |
| Continuous AC output | 2,400 W |
| RV outlet | Built-in 30A TT-30 |
| Price after discount | **$854.05** |
| Price per Wh | ~$0.42 |

The three biggest advantages:

1. **RV-friendly connection:** Built-in TT-30 outlet lets you connect a compatible RV shore-power cord directly, without needing a separate adapter setup.
2. **Good power capacity:** 2,400W continuous output can handle many RV essentials, including refrigerators, laptops, lights, and other appliances.
3. **Good price:** At $854.05, you get approximately 2kWh of LiFePO4 storage while staying below your $900 budget.

### Other contenders

Based on the supplied search results:

| Model | Capacity | Output | Price | Best for |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | **$854.05** | Best RV connection |
| Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 | ~2kWh | — | $899.99 | Lighter weight (41.7 lb) |
| Renogy PowerStation 2000 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | $849 | Budget-conscious RV owners |
| Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | 2,042Wh | 2,200W | $899 | Simple portable power |

<text color="secondary" size="xs">Prices and specifications are from the supplied search results; unavailable specifications are left blank.</text>

### One important caveat

The AC200L is an older model. The supplied results note that BLUETTI Canada lists it as discontinued, although the US store reportedly had stock on October 31, 2026.

Also, a built-in 30A RV outlet does not mean it can deliver the full 30A (3,600W) that a typical 120V RV hookup supports. Its 2,400W inverter is the limiting factor. Check your RV's air-conditioner startup requirements before buying.

---

## My final recommendation

**I'd buy the BLUETTI AC200L at $854.05**, provided the promotional price and stock are still available.

It offers the combination that matters most for RV use: approximately 2kWh capacity, 2,400W output, and a built-in TT-30 outlet.

If portability is more important than the built-in RV connection, I'd also consider the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2.
